> [source_metadata] [Printed page 480.][^MTP-AUDIT-C05-414]

<a id="mtp-000320"></a>
> [chapter_colophon] the fifth chapter, which teaches the natural state and delusion as self-complete.[^T05-049][^MTP-AUDIT-C05-414][^MTP-AUDIT-C05-415]

## Chapter 6

[Fixed chapter release](https://github.com/Lotus-King-Translation/Mu-Tig-Phreng-Ba/tree/translate-ch06-v1)

<a id="mtp-000321"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Electronic chapter marker 6.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-002]

<a id="mtp-000322"></a>
The holder of the vajra again petitioned:[^T06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003]

<a id="mtp-000323"></a>
“O, O great Vajradhara, Lord of Secret Mantra!  
The oneness of all buddhas—  
what is that very enlightened intent like?[^T06-001][^T06-002][^CH06-G001056][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-004][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-005][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-006]

<a id="mtp-000324"></a>
Through the stains of the five afflictions,  
how do sentient beings become bound?  
Bhagavān, speak to me.”[^T06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-007][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-008]

<a id="mtp-000325"></a>
The Bhagavān spoke:[^T06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-009]

<a id="mtp-000326"></a>
“As for the single truth of all buddhas,  
intrinsic nature, through essence,  
is distinguished from that itself.[^T06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-010][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-011][^T06-L001][^T06-L002]

<a id="mtp-000327"></a>
In the appearance of essence, primordial knowing,  
intrinsic nature pervades all, endowed with five embodiments.  
The result is the unique sphere.[^T06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-012][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-013][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-014][^T06-L002]

<a id="mtp-000328"></a>
In appearance itself there is union;[^T06-004][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-015][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-017]

<a id="mtp-000329"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 481.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-018][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-019]

<a id="mtp-000330"></a>
in emptiness there is clear light.[^T06-004][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-020]

<a id="mtp-000331"></a>
Essence itself is simultaneous;  
within intrinsic nature itself, [it is] gradual.[^T06-004][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-021][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-022]

<a id="mtp-000332"></a>
In the all-pervading, empty nature of phenomena,  
there is freedom from the dust of extremes.  
In the appearance of intrinsic nature, clear light,  
there is freedom from the stain of delusion.[^T06-005][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-023][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-024][^T06-L001][^T06-L002]

<a id="mtp-000333"></a>
In dharma embodiment, clear light, great bliss,  
the extremes of entities are empty.  
In the naturally arising king of awareness,  
[it is] beyond the domains of high and low.[^T06-005][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-025][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-026][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-027]

<a id="mtp-000334"></a>
I myself, from the enlightened intent of buddhas,  
am saṃsāra; I am nirvāṇa.  
I am phenomena; I am non-phenomena.[^T06-006][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-028][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-029][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-030][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000335"></a>
I am the lower destinies, hells and the like.  
I am mandalas, deities, and mantra.  
I am the precious ones, buddhas and the like.[^T06-006][^CH06-G001085][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-031][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-032][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-034][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000336"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 482.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-035][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-036]

<a id="mtp-000337"></a>
I am the teacher, retinue, and teaching.  
I am gathering—gathering my own retinue.  
I am view, cultivation, and activity.  
I am empowerment, commitments, and vows.[^T06-007][^CH06-G001089][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-037][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-039][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-040][^T06-L005]

<a id="mtp-000338"></a>
I am offerings, meditative stability, and deep absorption.  
I am washing, cleanliness, and stainlessness.  
I am virtuous and nonvirtuous activity.  
I am sūtra discourses, discipline, and higher doctrine.[^T06-008][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-041][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-042][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-043]

<a id="mtp-000339"></a>
I am the two truths, empty and not empty.  
I am the general and the distinctions of the vehicles.  
I am wrongdoing, action, and ripening.  
I am the world, its receptacle and contents.[^T06-009][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-044][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-045]

<a id="mtp-000340"></a>
Therefore I am what goes and what does not go.  
I am action and that itself, the stain of affliction.  
I am the faculties and objects.[^T06-009][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-046][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-047][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-048][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-049][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000341"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 483.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-050][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-051]

<a id="mtp-000342"></a>
I am the aggregates, elements, and sense bases.  
I am flesh, blood, and bone.  
I am names, letters, words, and forms.  
I am apprehended object and apprehending subject, objects, and conceptualizing a self.[^T06-010][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-048][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-052][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-053][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000343"></a>
I am suffering, ignorance, and delusion.  
I am sound, smell, taste, and touch.  
I am the mistaken apprehension of heat and cold.  
I am hunger, thirst, and bewilderment.  
I am pleasure, suffering, and equanimity.[^T06-011][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-048][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-054][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-055][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-056][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-057][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-058][^T06-L005]

<a id="mtp-000344"></a>
In brief, I am however [things] appear.  
I am undefeated, victorious over all.  
I have no contrived utterance; I am exalted beyond all.  
I have neither permanence nor annihilation; I enter in every manner.[^T06-012][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-048][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-059][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-060][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-061][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-062][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-063][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-064][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-065][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-066]

<a id="mtp-000345"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 484.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-067][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-068]

<a id="mtp-000346"></a>
I have no object of seeing; I appear manifestly to all.  
I am complete to the depths of everything; I am greater than all.  
I have no path to traverse; I have passed beyond all.  
I am unique; I am related to all.[^T06-013][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-065][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-069][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-070][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-071][^T06-L002][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000347"></a>
I have no ground on which to abide; I depend on all.  
I have no rival to compete with; I am unique among all.  
For me, insentient and aware are not two; I pervade all.  
I wear the clothing of darkness; I show appearance to all.[^T06-013][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-065][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-072][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-073][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-074][^T06-L002]

<a id="mtp-000348"></a>
Having made a རྒྱ་ཐེག of mountains, my strength is great.  
Through ཧུབ་ཀྱིས་སྟོབ་པས with the ocean, my ལྒོབ is great.  
Having put a mountain into a sesame seed, my deeds are great.[^T06-014][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-065][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-075][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-076][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-077][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-078][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-079]

<a id="mtp-000349"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 485.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-080][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-081]

<a id="mtp-000350"></a>
Having worn darkness as clothing, I am a great hero.  
Having traversed saṃsāra and nirvāṇa in one stride, my leap is great.  
Having pressed down the grounds at one time, my majesty is great.  
Having spread out the sun and moon as a seat, my splendor is great.[^T06-015][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-078][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-082][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-083][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-084][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-085]

<a id="mtp-000351"></a>
Because saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are complete in me at one time, I am free from doing.  
Because appearance arises unobstructedly in me, [it is] self-arising itself.  
Because realization and non-realization are absent in me, [I am] primordially buddha.  
Because hope and fear are absent in me, saṃsāra and nirvāṇa are complete at one time.[^T06-015][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-078][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-086][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-087][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-088][^T06-L005]

<a id="mtp-000352"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 486.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-089][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-090]

<a id="mtp-000353"></a>
Because ཡེ་ང and apprehension are absent in me, I am free from all fear.  
Because there is no master of contriving in me, [there is] letting be from the beginning.  
Because apprehended object and apprehending subject are not objects in me, [there is] self-abiding from the beginning.  
Because receptacle and contents are not two in me, everything is myself.  
Because bearers of phenomena and the nature of phenomena are absent in me, everything is one.”[^T06-016][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-092][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-093][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-094][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-095][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-096][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000354"></a>
The holder of the vajra again petitioned:[^T06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091]

<a id="mtp-000355"></a>
“If, in this way, all worldly phenomena of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa  
are one in essence,  
[—] is bound by sentient beings?[^T06-017][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-097][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-098][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-099][^T06-L001][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000356"></a>
If it is unfitting that those are bound,  
or is that itself unbound?  
Or is [it] bound by others?  
Bhagavān, སུངས to me.”[^T06-017][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-100][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-101][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-102][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000357"></a>
The Bhagavān spoke:[^T06-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091]

<a id="mtp-000358"></a>
“As for sentient beings’ five afflictions,[^T06-018][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-091][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-103][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-105][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000359"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 487.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-106][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-107]

<a id="mtp-000360"></a>
like clouds in space,  
[they] are accompanied by adventitious conditions.  
Those clouds arise from the state of space;  
when they likewise dissolve into space,  
[it] is called the state of inseparable oneness.[^T06-018][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-108][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-109][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-110]

<a id="mtp-000361"></a>
Likewise, [there is] no stain of affliction.  
If naturally arising intrinsic nature itself is known,  
how could sentient beings be bound?[^T06-018][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-111][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-112][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-113][^T06-L001][^T06-L003]

<a id="mtp-000362"></a>
If that itself is held as true,  
even buddhas themselves become bound;  
why would sentient beings not be bound?[^T06-019][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-114][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-115][^T06-L001]

<a id="mtp-000363"></a>
If [one] knows that there is no truth and no intrinsic nature,  
the stains are purified in their own place.  
Like turbidity in water becoming clear by itself,  
all phenomena are one in lacking intrinsic nature.[^T06-019][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-116][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-117][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-118][^T06-L001][^T06-L002][^T06-L003][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000364"></a>
If [one] does not know nonentity in this way,  
and, regarding the aggregates, elements, and sense bases,  
[one] holds through apprehended object and apprehending subject,[^T06-020][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-104][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-119][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-120][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-121][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-122][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-123][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000365"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 488.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-124][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-125]

<a id="mtp-000366"></a>
[one] abides for a long time in saṃsāra itself.  
In the house of the three realms,  
[one] enters the prison of name and form,  
bound with the iron of ignorance and action,[^T06-020][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-122][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-126][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-127][^T06-L004][^T06-L005]

<a id="mtp-000367"></a>
separated from the naturally arising lamp itself,  
covered by the thick darkness of saṃsāra,  
attached to the ལན་ཚའི་རོལ of desire,  
bound tightly by the noose of deluded dullness,[^T06-021][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-122][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-128][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-129][^T06-L003][^T06-L004]

<a id="mtp-000368"></a>
tormented by the heat of the fire of hatred,  
with the head wrapped in pride,  
obscured by the door of jealousy itself,[^T06-021][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-122][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-130][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-131][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-132]

<a id="mtp-000369"></a>
surrounded by an army of anger and the like,  
secured on right and left by mindfulness itself,  
and tied by the neck with the noose of apprehended object and apprehending subject.[^T06-021][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-122][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-133][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-134][^T06-L003]

<a id="mtp-000370"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 489.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-135][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-136]

<a id="mtp-000371"></a>
sinking into the mud of past and future habitual tendencies,  
joining hands with ripening itself,  
through action, mother and child, the intermediate state, and—  
through action, having linked mother and child,[^T06-022][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-138][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-139][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-140][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000372"></a>
from one to another, like buckets of water,  
[one] takes bodies in good and bad stages  
and is born into the respective families.[^T06-022][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-141][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-142][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-143]

<a id="mtp-000373"></a>
Having འབོགས into generations of grasping at “I,”  
[one] sinks into the depths of the ocean of suffering,  
held at the heart by the hook of the lower destinies.  
Oneself binds oneself: afflictions are the enemy.[^T06-023][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-144][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-145][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-146][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000374"></a>
For hell beings, [it] appears as fire and water;  
for hungry ghosts, [as] hunger and thirst;  
for animals, like ལན་བུན;[^T06-024][^CH06-G001199][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-147]

<a id="mtp-000375"></a>
for humans, [as] aggregates, elements,  
sense bases, and the five elements.  
That too is pleasure, suffering, and equanimity.[^T06-024][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-148][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-149][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-150][^T06-L007]

<a id="mtp-000376"></a>
For demigods, [it] appears as armor and weapons;  
for gods, [as] the qualities of desire.[^T06-024][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-137][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-151][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-152]

<a id="mtp-000377"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 490.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-153][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-154]

<a id="mtp-000378"></a>
Lord of Secrets, holder of the vajra!  
Those sentient beings in saṃsāra,  
although bound by their own differentiating conceptualization,  
are certain to be liberated because [it] lacks intrinsic nature,  
for, in the basic space of phenomena, [they] are even.[^T06-025][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-152][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-155][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-156][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-157][^T06-L006][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000379"></a>
The five aggregates, elements, and sense bases  
are liberated as families and lords of the families.  
The bearers of phenomena of apprehended object and apprehending subject  
are liberated as means and discerning knowing itself.[^T06-025][^CH06-G001216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-152][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-158][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-159][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-160][^T06-L007]

<a id="mtp-000380"></a>
Saṃsāra is liberated into the basic space of phenomena.  
The nature of phenomena is immeasurable, unimpeded penetration itself.  
The ultimate is unfixed, greatly open.  
[One] possesses the magical key of primordial knowing.[^T06-026][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-152][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-161][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-162][^T06-L008][^T06-L010]

<a id="mtp-000381"></a>
The lamp of clear light and emptiness is clear.  
Awareness, self-appearance, is a great light.  
[One] is not bound by attachment, like a snake’s knot.[^T06-026][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-152][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-163][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-164][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-166][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000382"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 491.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-167][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-168]

<a id="mtp-000383"></a>
Attached to the flavor of bliss in experiential acquaintance,  
[one’s] own body is bound by the noose of compassionate responsiveness.  
The fire of discerning knowing burns the afflictions;  
[one] also wears the clothing of great clear light.  
Having opened the treasury door of the nature of phenomena—[^T06-027][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-169][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-170][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-171][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-172][^T06-L006][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000384"></a>
an army’s force bears the weapon of self-awareness;  
the body rests on the two, view and activity;  
with the noose of conceptual thought, [one] is bound in saṃsāra.[^T06-027][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-173][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-174][^T06-L008][^T06-L010]

<a id="mtp-000385"></a>
The self-awareness of attachment appears before and after;  
the hand is joined with phenomena free from conceptualization.  
The two—mother and child of the nature of phenomena—meet.  
Self-awareness, primordial knowing, is unique.[^T06-027][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-175][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-176][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000386"></a>
Having found the object of great emptiness and clarity,  
[one] attains dharma embodiment without an apprehending subject,  
goes beyond the excellence of continuous deep absorption,  
and escapes from the expanse of the ocean of suffering.[^T06-028][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-177][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-178][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-179][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-180][^T06-L006][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000387"></a>
The enlightened intent of the means of secret mantra is one;  
primordial knowing is complete in primordial knowing itself.[^T06-028][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-165][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-181][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-182][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-183]

<a id="mtp-000388"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 492.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-184]

<a id="mtp-000389"></a>
Because ignorance itself is completely purified,  
[one] abides in dharma embodiment, great clear light.  
Within the intrinsic nature of great bliss,  
entities and nonentities have passed beyond sorrow.[^T06-029][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-182][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-185][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-186][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-187][^T06-L009]

<a id="mtp-000390"></a>
Empty primordial knowing is empty in essence.  
As for all-pervading intrinsic nature, primordial knowing,  
sound, smell, and taste have passed beyond sorrow.[^T06-029][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-182][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-188][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-189][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-190][^T06-L009]

<a id="mtp-000391"></a>
As for dharma embodiment without conceptual elaborations,  
form and consciousness have passed beyond sorrow.  
Because the primordial knowing of awareness pervades expansively,  
the entire three-thousandfold [world] has passed beyond sorrow.[^T06-029][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-182][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-191][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-192][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-193][^T06-L009]

<a id="mtp-000392"></a>
Because the basic space of phenomena is completely purified from the beginning,  
the five elements themselves have passed beyond sorrow.  
Because the single embodiment of buddhas pervades all,  
names and letters have passed beyond sorrow.[^T06-029][^CH06-G001256][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-182][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-194][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-195][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-196][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-197][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-198][^T06-L006][^T06-L007][^T06-L009]

<a id="mtp-000393"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 493.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-199]

<a id="mtp-000394"></a>
Through indestructible vajra primordial knowing,  
earth, stones, mountains, and rocks have passed beyond sorrow.  
In the nature of phenomena, free from conceptual elaborations,  
conventional designation itself has passed beyond sorrow.[^T06-029][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-201][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-202][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-203][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-204][^T06-L010]

<a id="mtp-000395"></a>
Emaho!  
This, from the perfectly [awakened] buddhas’  
very essence, has not moved:  
the unchanging nature of phenomena, utterly stable.[^T06-030][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-205][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-206][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-207]

<a id="mtp-000396"></a>
Self-appearance, self-liberation, one’s own object;  
intrinsic nature, self-purified, one’s own radiance;  
leaving as it is—leave, leave in itself.”[^T06-030][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-208][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-209][^T06-L008]

<a id="mtp-000397"></a>
Then those possessing vajras  
petitioned the Bhagavān in these words:[^T06-031][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000398"></a>
“Alas, Bhagavān Vajradhara!  
For all these worldly sentient beings,  
what is the ground on which they abide like?  
What is the path along which they go like?  
What sort of result do they attain?  
Vajradhara, speak to me.”[^T06-031][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-210][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-211][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000399"></a>
The Bhagavān spoke:[^T06-031][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-212][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000400"></a>
“Holder of the vajra, listen well!  
In this body of delusion accompanied by conceptualizing,[^T06-031][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-200][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-213][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-214][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000401"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 494.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-215]

<a id="mtp-000402"></a>
stainless and pure dharma embodiment  
abides in the manner of being left without being sought.[^T06-032][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-217][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-218][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-219][^T06-L009]

<a id="mtp-000403"></a>
As for the embodiments of buddhas themselves,  
the mandala of awakened mind is complete without being generated.  
As for the single embodiment without change,  
[it] abides in an all-pervading manner.[^T06-032][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-220][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-221][^T06-L006]

<a id="mtp-000404"></a>
The single ordinary mind that pervades everywhere  
abides in the genuine state of intrinsic nature.  
The embodiment of vajra—vajra chains—  
abides with its continuity unbroken.[^T06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-222][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-223][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-224][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-225]

<a id="mtp-000405"></a>
Because vajra chains are many in number,  
the embodiments of their portions are inconceivable.[^T06-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-226]

<a id="mtp-000406"></a>
In that there is nothing other than one,  
all appearances appear everywhere,  
endowed with the identity of emptiness and clarity.[^T06-034][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-216][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-227][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-228][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-229][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-231]

<a id="mtp-000407"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 495.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-232]

<a id="mtp-000408"></a>
That is the appearance of primordial knowing.  
The essence of embodiment is like that.[^T06-034][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-233][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-234]

<a id="mtp-000409"></a>
From the channels, there are spheres,  
endowed with a fine and darting identity,  
beautiful with rays of light.[^T06-035][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-235][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-236]

<a id="mtp-000410"></a>
These have three parts:  
right, left, and center.[^T06-035][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-237]

<a id="mtp-000411"></a>
The right, Roma, is the conventional sphere:  
a part of the limbs of great bliss.  
The source of gathered bliss  
is the great secret of all buddhas;  
[it is] intrinsic nature indicated by means.[^T06-035][^CH06-G001306][^CH06-G001307][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-238][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-239][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-240][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-241][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-242][^T06-L011]

<a id="mtp-000412"></a>
Endowed with the intrinsic nature of ultimate dharma embodiment,  
[it] abides as one sphere of emptiness-clarity.[^T06-035][^CH06-G001311][^CH06-G001312][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-230][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-243][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-244][^T06-L011]

<a id="mtp-000413"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 496.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-245]

<a id="mtp-000414"></a>
[It] abides within the center, and intrinsic nature is clear;  
[it] is beyond the objects of proliferating and gathering, speaking and thinking.  
Gently, [it is] free from differentiating conceptualization.  
The two extremes of existence and nonexistence are completely clear.[^T06-036][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-246][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-247][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-248][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-249][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-250][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-251][^T06-L011][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000415"></a>
There is no abiding at the limits of permanence and annihilation.  
Free from differentiating conceptualization, [there is] spontaneous presence.  
Without expression, [it is] naturally empty.  
[It is] the sphere of the ultimate entity.[^T06-036][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-246][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-252][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-253][^T06-L011][^T06-L015]

<a id="mtp-000416"></a>
On the left abides the sphere of intrinsic nature.  
Through bliss, union pervades both;  
without abiding utterly,  
through joining face to face, bliss is attained.[^T06-037][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-246][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-254][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-255][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-256][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-257][^T06-L011]

<a id="mtp-000417"></a>
[It is] the cause of Mahamudra itself,  
the path of great bliss, great primordial knowing,  
the mandala, lord of all secret mantra.[^T06-037][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-246][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-258][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-259][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-261][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-262][^T06-L011]

<a id="mtp-000418"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 497.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-263]

<a id="mtp-000419"></a>
[It is] the great means that rescues saṃsāra,  
the light blazing with the primordial radiance of secrecy.  
That is the essence of great bliss.[^T06-037][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-264][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-265][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-266][^T06-L011]

<a id="mtp-000420"></a>
The path of going is the gate that enables seeing.  
That itself: two on the right, two on the left, and the center,  
abides in the manner of a blazing lamp.[^T06-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-267][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-268][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-269][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000421"></a>
The lamp of the empty sphere,  
the lamp of pure basic space,  
naturally arising discerning knowing itself,  
and the water lamp of the far-reaching lasso  
appear to the objects of seeing.[^T06-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-270][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-271][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-272][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-273][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-274]

<a id="mtp-000422"></a>
Awareness, free from conceptualization, vajra chains,  
appears from the gate of Brahmā, great bliss,  
like the luster of a peacock.[^T06-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-275][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-276][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-277]

<a id="mtp-000423"></a>
Thig: there is no change;[^T06-039][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-260][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-278][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-279][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-280][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-281]

<a id="mtp-000424"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 498.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-282]

<a id="mtp-000425"></a>
le pervades and appears to objects.  
The lamp transforms darkness into appearance.[^T06-039][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-279][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-283][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000426"></a>
Like a rainbow in space,  
through purity the stains of affliction are exhausted.  
Basic space is vast, and its extent is unbroken.  
Because the nature of phenomena is completely pure in the object,  
[it] causes arising from the corners of both.  
The pervading blue is unchanging.[^T06-040][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-279][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-284][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-285][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-286][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-287][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-288][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000427"></a>
If [it] meets the conditions of pure appearance,  
[it] becomes endowed with five colors.[^T06-040][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-279][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-289][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-290][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000428"></a>
Like a burning fire-lamp,  
knowing realizes phenomena simultaneously.  
Rab becomes the summit of all.  
Rang is free from phenomena dependent on others.  
Byung ba, unobstructed, appears in letting be.  
From the left, the gate that enables arising is unceasing.[^T06-041][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-279][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-291][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-292][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-293][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-294][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-295][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-296][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-298][^T06-L012]

<a id="mtp-000429"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 499.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-299]

<a id="mtp-000430"></a>
Like a hook that apprehends,  
the continuum, on the stallion of the five gates—  
mental consciousness mounts and moves,  
entering all objects and gathering.[^T06-042][^CH06-G001364][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-300][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-301][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-302][^T06-L012][^T06-L013][^T06-L015]

<a id="mtp-000431"></a>
“Lasso”: to the very objects of the apprehended object,  
the ordinary mind of the apprehending subject fully apprehends.[^T06-042][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297]

<a id="mtp-000432"></a>
“Water” distinguishes the clear from the sediment.  
Moreover, in the two the portions are equal.  
In brief, [it] is the refined essence of the faculties.[^T06-042][^CH06-G001371][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-303][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-304][^T06-L013]

<a id="mtp-000433"></a>
For example, like a gold chain  
well strung by a skilled craftsman,  
awareness knows and is aware of everything.  
Free from conceptualization, [it] is unstained by saṃsāra.  
Vajra chains are connected in succession.  
The opening of great bliss is the path free from conceptualization.[^T06-043][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-305][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-306][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-307][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-308][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-309][^T06-L013]

<a id="mtp-000434"></a>
The result is said to be two རྣལ་བ:  
unripened saṃsāra itself,  
and the liberating embodiments and primordial knowing.[^T06-044][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-310][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-311][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-312][^T06-L013]

<a id="mtp-000435"></a>
Those, moreover, are encompassed by the four births:[^T06-044][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-297]

<a id="mtp-000436"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 500.][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-313]

<a id="mtp-000437"></a>
gods, demigods, humans,  
animals, hungry ghosts,  
and likewise the world of hells  
appear as forms from the unripened.[^T06-044][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-314][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-315][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-316][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-317][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-318][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-319][^T06-L013]

unelaborated by conceptual elaborations.[^T06-046][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-330][^MTP-AUDIT-C06-334][^T06-L014]

<a id="mtp-000445"></a>

<a id="mtp-000446"></a>

<a id="mtp-000454"></a>
Then the holder of the vajra  
petitioned Vajradhara in these words:[^T07-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-003]

<a id="mtp-000455"></a>
“Are sentient beings and the phenomena of saṃsāra and nirvāṇa

<a id="mtp-000456"></a>
Then that great Vajradhara  
rose from the seat of bliss  
and solemnly uttered these words:[^T07-001][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-006][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-007]

<a id="mtp-000457"></a>
“The phenomena of saṃsāra are like this:  
since this is absent [at] the very beginning,  
just as imputed through delusion about objects,  
[they] appear within the domain of sentient beings.[^T07-001][^T07-002][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-008][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-009]

<a id="mtp-000458"></a>

earth, water, fire and wind;[^T07-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-012][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-013]

> [source_metadata] [Printed page 503.][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-010][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-011]

<a id="mtp-000460"></a>
space, sun and moon;  
the [གཟུངས: unresolved] of males and females;  
planets, stars and clouds;  
trees, mountains and rocks;[^T07-003][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-012][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-014][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-015]

<a id="mtp-000461"></a>

<a id="mtp-000464"></a>
Earth is flesh, entity itself.  
Water is blood, gathering itself.  
Fire is heat, ripening the entire body.  
Wind is breath, holding the body’s vitality.

<a id="mtp-000465"></a>
Sun and moon are eyes, making clear.

<a id="mtp-000466"></a>
Planets are the mouth, and stars are teeth.

<a id="mtp-000468"></a>
Mountains are the body, and rocks are bones.

<a id="mtp-000470"></a>

<a id="mtp-000474"></a>

<a id="mtp-000476"></a>
Music is the complete maṇḍala of the five lights.

maṇḍalas, deities and offerings;

view, activity and cultivation;

<a id="mtp-000483"></a>
Within means and discerning knowing themselves, moreover:

emptiness and the absence of conceptual elaborations;

suffering, origin and cessation,

<a id="mtp-000491"></a>
The holder of the vajra again petitioned:[^T07-024][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-109]

<a id="mtp-000492"></a>
“Within the basic space of phenomena, equal to space,

<a id="mtp-000495"></a>

<a id="mtp-000496"></a>

<a id="mtp-000497"></a>
Since uttering, speaking and thinking have no object,[^T07-028][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-109]

<a id="mtp-000499"></a>
all are the words of one’s own mantra.[^T07-028][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-120][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-121]

<a id="mtp-000501"></a>

<a id="mtp-000502"></a>

<a id="mtp-000503"></a>
Since the three embodiments are primordially complete without being generated,

<a id="mtp-000504"></a>

<a id="mtp-000505"></a>
As for the sounds of varied appearances,

[it is] beyond the object of reflection and examination.[^T07-033][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-120][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-130][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-133][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-147]

<a id="mtp-000506"></a>
> [source_metadata] [Printed page 511.][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-131][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-132]

<a id="mtp-000507"></a>
Since primordial knowing of awareness is primordially radiant,  
[it is] liberated from words of cultivating and contriving.

<a id="mtp-000508"></a>
Since appearances are left in naked resting,

<a id="mtp-000509"></a>

Since self-awareness is free of the stain of differentiating conceptualization,  
unobscured ethical discipline is one’s own body.[^T07-036][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-133][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-139][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-140][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-141][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-142]

<a id="mtp-000510"></a>

Since [there is] primordial awareness and freedom from thinking,[^T07-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-133][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-166][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-280]

qualities are complete, and ordinary mind itself is shown.[^T07-038][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-167][^MTP-AUDIT-C07-280]

<a id="mtp-000515"></a>

<a id="mtp-000517"></a>

<a id="mtp-000519"></a>

<a id="mtp-000520"></a>

<a id="mtp-000521"></a>

## Endnotes

[^T01-001]: Golden-v1, chapter 1, printed 417–418, 423, MTP-S000004, MTP-S000008, MTP-S000096. Tibetan: རྒྱུད. The canonical assignment is “continuum.” These occurrences name the present text, two in title formulas with ཅེས་བྱ་བ and one in the chapter colophon. “Tantra” is an occurrence-specific, provisional text-genre rendering; the canonical entry remains unchanged, and this choice does not govern other uses of རྒྱུད. Review action: approve or replace this title/colophon usage. The full opening title retains “precious,” while the shorter colophon title does not add it.

[^T01-002]: Golden-v1, chapter 1, printed 418–419, MTP-S000009, MTP-S000011, MTP-S000014. Tibetan: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས; རིག་པའི་བདག་ཉིད; འཁྲུལ་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་རྣམས; འཁྲུལ་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་ཅན. The honorific is represented by the conventional name Bhagavān, provisionally, without claiming a Sanskrit source reading. The unlisted བདག་ཉིད is provisionally “very identity” or “identity”; ཅན is retained as “has.” This avoids silently assigning the reserved “essence” (ངོ་བོ) or “embodiment” (སྐུ) to a different source expression. The relation may instead concern personification or essential character; the source alone does not settle a universal English equivalent. Review these three constructions together; do not infer a permanent mapping.

[^T01-003]: Golden-v1, chapter 1, printed 418, 420, MTP-S000010, MTP-S000024. Tibetan: འདི་སྐད་བདག་གིས་བསྟན་པའི་དུས་གཅིག་ན / འདི་སྐད་བདག་གིས་ཐོས་པའི་དུས་གཅིག་ན. The first formula has བསྟན, “taught,” whereas the second has ཐོས, “heard.” The English preserves the first-person agent in both and does not regularize the first to the familiar hearing formula. The temporal construction is translated provisionally as “at one time when I taught” in the first formula and “Thus did I hear at one time” in the second. Review the temporal attachment and quotation punctuation; no source verb has been changed.

[^T01-004]: Golden-v1, chapter 1, printed 418–419, MTP-S000012, MTP-S000013, MTP-S000014. Tibetan: ང་མེད་པའི་སྔོན་རོལ་ན / འཁྲུལ་པ་མེད་པའི་རིག་པ / འཁྲུལ་པའི་བདག་ཉིད་ཅན་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཡོད་དེ. The overt negation in ང་མེད་པའི་སྔོན་རོལ་ན qualifies the phrase governed by “before.” The revised draft therefore keeps the literal, temporally difficult “Before my nonexistence.” The earlier “Before I was” hid or reversed that scope and is preserved only in revisions/translation-draft-01.md. Neither a prior-existence narrative nor a philosophical no-self reading is established; the temporal relation remains unresolved. The next clauses call awareness free from delusion “that which has the identity of delusion.” This apparent tension is retained; neither a negation nor a different speaker is supplied. Review the relation of the name to awareness and the temporal phrase against the full source context. The working syntax is provisional, not an emendation.

[^T02-001]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000099–S000107, S000142, S000166, S000220–S000221 (printed 423, 425–426, 429). Names and whole expressions: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས / བཅོམ་ལྡན → “Bhagavān”; གསང་བའི་བདག་པོ / གསང་བའི་བདག → “Lord of Secrets”; རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ → “Vajrasattva”; རྟ་མགྲིན → “Hayagrīva”; གཤིན་རྗེ → “Lord of Death”; སེམས་ཅན → “sentient beings”; ཁྲོ་བོ → “wrathful ones”; རིགས → “family”; འཁོར་བ → “saṃsāra”; རྒྱུད in the title → “tantra”; མུ་ཏིག་ཕྲེང་བ → “The String of Pearls.” These occurrence-specific treatments continue chapter 1 but remain proposals, not approved additions. Name/whole-expression boundaries prevent mechanically inserting “ordinary mind” inside Vajrasattva or “continuum” in the tantra title; the standalone assignments remain intact. In S99 the phrase འཁྲུལ་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་དག་པའི་མངའ་བདག is provisionally “the sovereign in whom all delusion is pure”; “in whom” makes the compressed attachment explicit rather than changing “pure” to an unexpressed act of purification. S166’s double royal expression is retained as “King of the Lord of Death”; whether it should idiomatically be “King, Lord of Death” remains open. Review these scoped forms and attachments before glossary activation.

[^T02-002]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000108, S000113, S000123, S000140, S000145, S000152, S000158, S000221 (printed 423–429). The ལྡོག / བཟློག family is provisionally “reverse/turn back/return,” according to the expressed subject and case. Preserve the direction distinctions: གཞི་ལ (“in/to the Ground”), མ་ལ (“in/to the mother”), but the colophon གཞི་ལས (“from the Ground”). “Reversing Delusion from the Ground” retains the ablative rather than silently assimilating the title to the earlier locatives; “reversing delusion at its basis” is a possible contextual interpretation requiring review. “The Ground” follows the established གཞི entry, with “the Ground” in prose as in chapter 1; its internal capitalization remains a presentation choice rather than a glossary amendment. These locatives do not by themselves settle whether delusion dissolves into the Ground or is reversed there.

[^T02-021]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000194–S000202 (printed 428). བདག་མེད is provisionally “without a self,” without extending the title’s “sovereign” sense to this negation. [^T02-025]: Golden-v1, chapter 2 (printed 424–429), occurrences identified exactly in usage.json. Further recurring technical gaps are provisionally handled as follows: ཡུལ → “object”; standalone ཆོས → “phenomena,” with the scriptural S217 construction “teachings”; ངང → “state”; གཉིས་མེད → “nondual/nonduality”; standalone སངས → “cleared away”; རྒྱུན → “flow” in the gate/mindfulness constructions, “continuity” in S171 and S191; དངོས་པོ → “entity”; དངོས་མེད → “without substance”; adverbial དངོས in S161/S213 → “in actuality.” The last family has distinct constructions whose equivalence is not assumed. Full compounds such as ཆོས་ཉིད, ཆོས་སྐུ, and གཟུང་བ retain their established full mappings and are not independently decomposed. In particular “object” does not erase the specifically assigned apprehended-object role. སངས does not acquire the established complete རང་སངས → self-purified mapping by substring. རྒྱུན stays distinct from canonical རྒྱུད → continuum. “Without substance” concerns the adjectival negation, not an approved new entity definition. These are minimum occurrence-specific proposals following full-table searches and neighboring-entry checks; review each construction before any glossary addition. All repeated local uses remain traceable in the usage record, not silently promoted to defaults.

[^T03-001]: Golden-v1, chapter 3, MTP-S000223–S000341 (printed 429–436). Names and whole expressions remain occurrence-specific proposals: རྟ་མགྲིན → “Hayagrīva”; ཁྲོ་བོ → “wrathful ones”; བཅོམ་ལྡན → “Bhagavān”; རྡོ་རྗེ་འཆང → “Vajradhara”; གསང་བདག / གསང་བའི་བདག་པོ → “Lord of Secrets”; རྡོ་རྗེ་འཛིན → “holder of the vajra”; སངས་རྒྱས → “buddha”; སེམས་ཅན → “sentient beings”; མྱ་ངན་འདས → “nirvāṇa.” The differently written vajra titles are not silently normalized into one source form. Proper-name and whole-expression treatment does not weaken standalone སེམས → ordinary mind or འཛིན་པ → apprehending subject. These proposals follow the complete current glossary and chapter 1–2 usage review but inherit no owner approval from prior drafting. Review the proper-name identification and whole-expression bounds before activation.

[^T03-002]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000224–S000226 (printed 429): རང་རིག་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཆེན་པོའི་ལུང / ངེས་པའི་རྒྱལ་པོས་བཀའ་སྩོལ་ཅིག. “Authoritative teaching” is proposed for ལུང; scripture or authoritative pronouncement is also possible. The draft takes ངེས་པའི་རྒྱལ་པོས as the honorific agent addressed, “king of certainty,” rather than making certainty a modifier of the teaching. “[It]” resumes the preceding object in English. ཆེན་པོ qualifies primordial knowing in the working reading. Review these attachments and the authority-term; the three lines do not identify a separate scripture by name.

[^T03-003]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000227–S000232 (printed 429): མ་བཞུགས་པ་ཡི་སྟན་ལས་ལངས retains the negation in “arose from the seat where he did not abide.” Its apparent paradox is not repaired to “where he sat”; another attachment of མ་བཞུགས is possible but not securely established. The formula སར་བ་འདུས་ཧ is retained exactly in Tibetan, followed by the translated utterance/address sequence. The native audit and golden record both leave its stacks/encoding uncertain; no Sanskrit reconstruction, corrected spelling, or invented meaning is supplied. “Word-formula” preserves the སྒྲ → word assignment and labels the utterance’s function; formula is an editorial classification. S232 སྣང་བྱེད is “makes [things] appear,” a grammatical realization of appearance, with the unspecified object visibly supplied. Review the seat syntax and formula encoding separately; the pair containing the formula is locally unresolved, not wholly untranslated.

[^T03-004]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000225, S000235, S000283, S000297, S000299, S000338 (printed 429–436). རང་རིག is provisionally “self-awareness,” retaining awareness and remaining distinct from established self-recognition. The genitive “self-awareness’s … primordial knowing” is one interpretation of juxtaposition; apposition is possible. In S283 རང་རིག་འོད་སྣང, “light-appearance of self-awareness” preserves both light and appearance without silently turning the phrase into canonical clear light. S297 སེམས་ཉིད is “ordinary mind itself”; it is not silently changed to generic “nature of mind.” A technical whole-expression decision for སེམས་ཉིད remains open, and the force of སྣ་ཚོགས (“varied”) is retained. Review these uncovered compounds rather than inferring approval from earlier chapters.

[^T03-005]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000234–S000237 (printed 430): ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་དང་དབྱེར་མེད་པས / རང་རིག་ཡུལ་གྱི་སྤྱོད་ལམ་ནི / ཐབས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ལས་ཤེས་རབ་ཉིད / འགག་མེད་ཀློང་དུ་ཐམས་ཅད་རོལ. “[It]” in the first line refers provisionally to the blazing lamp introduced before the page marker. “Way of activity” preserves the activity component in unglossaried སྤྱོད་ལམ; it is not an approved whole-expression assignment. The draft leaves “from the embodiment of means, discerning knowing itself” as a compressed nominal construction rather than inserting an unsupported transformation verb. The exact scope of ཐམས་ཅད and its relation to discerning knowing remain open. འགག་མེད is linked provisionally to the unceasing family, and རོལ to established play. Review the genitive/ablative relations and the subject of play together.

[^T03-006]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000238–S000242 (printed 430): རང་བཞིན་སྣང་བ་མ་འགགས་པ / ངོ་བོ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་སྐུ་ལྟར་འཕྲོ. “The unceasing appearance of intrinsic nature” provisionally supplies a genitive relation; “intrinsic nature—unceasing appearance” is an alternative. The full intrinsic-nature expression remains identifiable, and “like” preserves ལྟར instead of asserting identity. “Proliferates” is the grammatical realization of established འཕྲོ. In ཆོས་ཉིད་ཡུལ་ལ་གཟིགས་སྣང་མཁྱེན, “[it] sees and knows appearance in the object of the nature of phenomena” is a provisional coordination of the honorific verbs. A reading involving “the appearance seen” is possible; the subject is not securely explicit. Review that syntax. བྱ་བྱེད continues the proposed “doing and the doer” pair, not an approved new compound.

[^T03-007]: Golden-v1, MTP-S000243–S000247 (printed 430): སྒྲོན་མའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་ཐིག་ལེ་གསལ. “The sphere of the lamp’s primordial knowing is clear” treats the middle juxtaposition as a genitive relation; “the lamp’s primordial knowing—the sphere is clear” is another possible division. [^T04-001]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S343/S348/S351/S370/S390 (printed436–438): names and titles are locally provisional whole expressions. རྟ་མགྲིན is Hayagrīva; exact S343 དབང་གིས་རྒྱལ་པོས is rendered “the king of power,” with the anomalous instrumental-looking གིས left uncorrected; compare shorter S351 དབང་རྒྱལ. བཅོམ་ལྡན is Bhagavān, while S348 རྡོ་རྗེ་དཔའ་བོ is “vajra hero,” not silently expanded to S370/S390 རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ, Vajrasattva. These names are not entries in the active glossary. Review the S343 epithet/case construction; no canonical mind or embodiment term is globally replaced by a name mapping.

[^T04-002]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S343–S485: recurring technical gaps remain local proposals, not approved glossary additions. The source forms རང་རིག, ཆོས, ཡུལ, ཐབས, ངང, སངས་རྒྱས, སེམས་ཅན, གསང་སྔགས, མན་ངག, མཚན་མ, སྙིང་པོ, དངོས་པོ, ཉོན་མོངས, and ཁམས are rendered self-awareness, phenomena, object, means, state, buddha, sentient beings, secret mantra, pith instruction, marks, core, entities, afflictions, and realms, respectively, only where their local construction supports them. ཡང་དག is provisionally authentic; standalone རང་བྱུང is naturally arising/natural arising, following the visible family in canonical རང་བྱུང་ཡེ་ཤེས without treating its component as a separately approved entry. The usage records give exact per-occurrence forms and narrower constructions; other notes describe material ambiguity. Ordinary mind, awareness, primordial knowing, discerning knowing, essence, intrinsic nature, and the listed whole expressions retain their established assignments. No list of five roots, faculties, or afflictions is supplied beyond the source. These local usages require review before glossary activation.

[^T04-003]: Golden-v1 S344–S346 (printed436): ཐུགས་རྗེ་ཅན keeps the established whole term compassionate responsiveness through “endowed with.” བདག་ཅག་རང་རིག་རྗེས་མཐུན་ལ is provisionally “in accord with our self-awareness”; the relation of རྗེས་མཐུན་ལ to the request is compressed and could instead characterize the recipients as conforming to self-awareness. ཆོས་ཉིད་དབྱིངས is treated as basic space of the nature of phenomena, retaining both established components rather than substituting the distinct whole entry ཆོས་དབྱིངས. The relational wording remains for review.

[^T04-004]: Golden-v1 S351–S371 and S485: quotation boundaries in English are editorial presentation. The first address is closed after S367; S368–S370, ending བཅོམ་ལྡན་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔས་བསྟན, is treated as a third-person teaching introduction; speech reopens at ཨེ་མ་ཧོ and closes before the clear narrative at S486. Reading S368–S370 as third-person wording within continuing speech remains possible. Neither the source nor a speaker’s identity is silently rewritten. Emaho preserves the exclamation provisionally rather than inventing explanatory content.

[^T04-005]: Golden-v1 S353–S356 (printed436): exact སངས་རྒྱས་སེམས་ཅན་ཀུན་གྱི་དུར / ཐེམ་ཞིང is retained locally because its attachment and compound division remain unresolved. དུར can suggest a grave/burial expression, and ཐེམ can suggest a threshold or another verbal/nominal reading, but neither establishes a secure combined phrase here. The surrounding causal clause, embodiment of primordial knowing, genitive “of all buddhas and sentient beings,” and action ཡང་དག་དོན་ལ་སྤྱོད are represented. “Acts” is the grammatical activity-family realization; authentic is provisional for ཡང་དག. Do not repair to a familiar doctrinal expression or absorb the untranscribed smaller annotation. Human lexical/syntax review of the preserved division is needed.

[^T04-006]: Golden-v1 S357–S362 (printed436–437): སྐྱེ་མེད is the shortened non-arising expression, not an independently chosen synonym. The sentence continues across the page label into the two distinct terms སྐྱེ་བྱ / སྐྱེ་བྱེད, provisionally “what arises / what brings about arising.” For exact ཐུགས་རྗེས་ཆོས་ཤིང་བཅད་དུ་མེད, the draft tentatively construes ཆོས as a shaping/ordering verb and the preceding embodiment/state as its recipients: “are shaped by compassionate responsiveness and cannot be cut off.” The verb and attachment remain uncertain; this is not a correction to བཅོས or a claim that every ཆོས means shaping. The negative cutting predicate is retained. Review the construction before treating this local verb sense as settled.

[^T04-007]: Golden-v1 S363–S367 (printed437): the string of nominal expressions is rendered as a provisional appositional sequence; the source does not express a copula for every line. In སྐུ་ཡི་ངོ་བོ་ལུ་གུ་རྒྱུད the embodiment/essence relation is explicit, while vajra chains is the established whole-expression assignment supported here by the spheres/light sequence. The source’s five rays are retained without naming a fivefold taxonomy. The final ལམ་གྱི་སྐུ remains “embodiment of the path”; a fuller relation among these descriptions awaits review.

[^T04-008]: Golden-v1 S368–S384 (printed437–438): དཀྱིལ་འཁོར is locally mandala, and སྤྲོས་པ་མེད་པ is provisionally “without conceptual elaborations,” preserving the family of canonical སྤྲོས་བྲལ without claiming exact identity. ལྷུན་འབྱམས is “spontaneously vast,” not canonical spontaneous presence for ལྷུན་གྲུབ. The full verb expression དོན་བྱེད is provisionally “serves purposes”; this context-specific action is not ordinary inflection of canonical meaning for standalone དོན. S376’s causal clause continues at S378. In S378–S379, the retained “plays in the space of empty primordial knowing” tentatively takes སྟོང་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་མཁའ as a compound nominal space phrase and carries the preceding expanse forward as subject; the Tibetan does not express an additional genitive between primordial knowing and space. The alternative “empty primordial knowing plays in space” changes subject and attachment and remains possible. This relational supply is not settled by the English and requires review. མཁའ is the short space form, distinct from basic space; ཏིང་འཛིན is a shortened deep-absorption expression. In S383–S384 the supplied “means of” and “is an” organize compressed nominal juxtaposition; an appositional reading remains possible. The repeated authentic primordial knowing at S380/S382 and the fire/wind comparisons are preserved without harmonization.

[^T04-009]: Golden-v1 S385–S388 (printed438): exact ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ is an expanded genitive realization of canonical dharma embodiment, not the canonical spelling itself. The first two lines are provisionally equated; དང then introduces the spheres’ abiding place. ངང་གིས is rendered naturally in this local adverbial construction, not as a universal replacement for the provisional nominal state. The distinct negatives མ་གཡོས / གཡོ་བ་མེད remain “unmoved / without movement.” Review whether the final predicate also scopes over the activity phrases.

[^T04-010]: Golden-v1 S389–S394 (printed438): the three causal endings as provisionally construed and the implicit subject of appearance/play are retained rather than replaced by a named agent. “In the state” tentatively relates the nominal S390 to the following showing clause. རྒྱུན་ཏུ means continuously locally; its spelling is not རྒྱུད, whose established assignment is continuum. ཡིད་ཆེས་གསུམ is provisionally “the three assurances,” an uncovered whole expression, not a general shortening of mental faculty or a named taxonomy supplied from elsewhere. Its count, instrument, and open referent require review.

[^T04-011]: Golden-v1 S396–S400 (printed439): སྤྱོད་པ་མ་སྤྱད preserves both the activity noun and its negative verbal counterpart as “without enacting activity.” Canonical རང་སར་གྲོལ remains liberated in its own place. S398–S400 is a compressed modifier chain: the draft takes appearances like embodiment through means as those abiding on the secret-mantra path and described as beyond thinking, utterly pure, beyond objects. Final ཡི links into those descriptions; the exact attachment remains provisional. “Like” is preserved rather than silently changed to identity. No source object or negative is omitted.

[^T04-012]: Golden-v1 S401–S407 (printed439): nominal apposition in ཆགས་མེད་ཡེ་ཤེས་གསུང་གི་ངང is represented by dashes, with speech distinct from embodiment. ལྷུན་རྫོགས is provisionally spontaneous completeness/spontaneously complete, not the separate canonical spontaneous presence; མཉམ་སྦྱོར is locally joins equally. In S406 ཐུགས་རྗེ་དྲི་མ་རྣམ་པར་དག the draft supplies “with” to leave the relation between compassionate responsiveness and completely pure stains visible without asserting an explicit genitive absent from the source. The implied subject continuing to “becoming great discerning knowing” is not named. Review the precise coordination; the canonical compassionate responsiveness and discerning knowing terms remain intact.

[^T04-013]: Golden-v1 S408–S418 (printed439–440): naturally arising primordial knowing is recognizable despite the source’s reordered ཡེ་ཤེས་རང་བྱུང; standalone natural arising remains proposed. The root/state relation and lamp/seal descriptions are provisionally read as nominal equations. S414 is rendered with dharma embodiment as subject and དངོས་པོའི་ལམ་དུ as “on the path of entities”; taking it as the continuation of the preceding nominal series is also possible. གནད་དུ་བརྡེག is provisionally “strikes the vital point,” and སྤྱི་བཅིངས is provisionally verbal “binds all together,” rather than canonical total immersion for the different སྤྱི་བླུགས. The king/pith-instruction relation is likewise compact. These construction choices require review; no source clause has been silently repaired.

[^T04-014]: Golden-v1 S419–S423 (printed440): exact སེམས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་བཅད་རྣམ་རྟོག་དངས is provisionally a description, “the gate of ordinary mind is closed; differentiating conceptualization clears.” An imperative construction is possible. དངས is retained as the source’s distinct clearing verb, not silently changed to གསལ or a different spelling. The metaphor ཁྱིམ་ཡངས་ཕུགས་རྡིབ is kept as “a spacious house, a collapsed interior,” without identifying an allegorical referent or adding a wall. S423 retains the closure of desire’s gate and clarity within. རྣལ་འབྱོར is locally yoga; whether the phrase points to practices or practitioners remains open. Review the metaphor and statement/instruction force; preserve the protected ordinary mind and differentiating conceptualization terms.

[^T04-128]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S607,S608,S609,S610,S611,S612,S613,S614 (printed452): S607–610 is a compressed conception/realization construction. Those causes are provisionally the subject moved by the propelling wind and described by awakening, self-awareness, great bliss. No semen, ovum, biological mechanism, or deity is added. ཐབས means and ཤེས་རབ discerning knowing remain distinct. The causal and appositional attachments require human review.

[^T04-129]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S611,S612,S613,S614 (printed452): S611–614 retains seed, five elements, the object of emptiness, and the bliss of two. སྙོམས་འཇུག is provisionally absorption, a separate unlisted expression, not silently identified with ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན deep absorption or མཉམ་གཞག equipoise. Sexual union is a plausible contextual sense but not substituted without a usage decision. The number two is not replaced by named participants within the English line.

[^T04-130]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S616,S617,S618,S619 (printed453): S616–619 preserves entry into the womb and the exact adjacent numerical claims. བདུན་ཚན་བདུན་གྱི་རྟོགས་ཚད is provisionally the measure of realization of seven groups of seven; seven weeks is plausible, but no time unit is inserted as if written. ཟླ་བཅུ is ten months, followed by traversing the levels. No arithmetic or biological harmonization reconciles these statements. ས here is levels, not the separate canonical གཞི The Ground. Existing golden smaller-annotation limits remain in force.

S625 ཤི་བས is read causally/instrumentally through death; [one] and the goal into are supplied to make the ellipsis readable. No claim that illness proves realization is added beyond the speaker’s actual statement.

[^T04-132]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S626,S627,S628,S629 (printed453): S628 is exactly ཨེ་མ་སྤྱོད་བསམ་བསྒྱུར་སྣང་བ་གྲོལ. In particular, no negative particle is inserted to match the following negative parallels. [^T04-133]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S631,S632,S633 (printed454): S631 རྟག་ཆད is provisionally permanence and annihilation; doctrinal eternalism/nihilism labels are not imposed. This regular case parsing does not require changing the fixed spelling. An alternative lexical reading of རྒྱས as fullness/expansion remains possible. Seal is locally proposed terminology consistent with the earlier chapter, not a canonical glossary addition.

[^T04-134]: Golden-v1, chapter 4, S634,S635 (printed454): Title and genre follow the prior chapter’s proposed local practice: མུ་ཏིག་ཕྲེང་བ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ Precious String of Pearls, and textual རྒྱུད Tantra. The source does not call the work secret in this chapter’s colophon, so secret is not added.

[^T05-001]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S637, S638, S639, S640, S649, S650, S654, S736, S739, S766 (printed 454–461). Names and titles are provisional whole expressions, not additions to the canonical glossary: ཁྲོ་བོ / ཁྲོ་བདག are wrathful ones / lord of wrathful ones; རིགས here is families, with no named taxonomy supplied; བཅོམ་ལྡན is Bhagavān; རྡོ་རྗེ་འཆང is Vajradhara. The distinct རྡོ་རྗེ་འཛིན is holder of the vajra, not an automatic application of apprehending subject to every འཛིན compound. གསང་བ་མཆོག་བདག is provisionally Supreme Lord of Secrets. སངས་རྒྱས / སེམས་ཅན are buddhas / sentient beings; the latter is a whole expression and does not replace standalone ordinary mind. At S654, ཀུན་བདག is read as lord of all in apposition to the one mandala; exact attachment remains for review. Quotation boundaries are editorial presentation.

[^T05-002]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S639, S640, S641, S642, S643, S644, S645, S646, S647 (printed 454). The questions are not silently answered or normalized. S639 རང་བཞིན་གང is read interrogatively as “what is the intrinsic nature”; a relative reading, “the intrinsic nature which ...,” is also possible. S643 repeats གང twice and the English preserves that repetition without identifying two means. S645 བདག་ཅག་རྣམས་ནི་གྱུར་ན has no securely supplied complement: “If we have become [—]” remains locally unresolved. “Become that primordial knowing” would be a reconstruction from context, not overt wording. S646 གཉིས་སྣང is provisionally twofold appearance; what the two are is not supplied. Review the interrogative attachment and missing complement against the source layers.

[^T05-003]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S650, S651, S652, S653, S654 (printed 455). S651 exact གཉིས་ནི་གཞི་ངོ་བོ་གཅིག་ཁྱད་པར་ལས is preserved as a compressed sequence: “The two—the Ground, one in essence; from distinction—”. The referent of “two,” the attachment of ཁྱད་པར་ལས, and the subject of S652 གནས remain unsettled. The English does not insert a causal origin story or remove the expanded words. S652 སྤྲོས་མེད is provisionally without conceptual elaborations, preserving the family of canonical སྤྲོས་བྲལ without claiming an exact entry. S653 བདེ་ཆེན is great bliss; S654 དཀྱིལ་འཁོར is mandala, both local proposals. The following descriptions are provisionally appositional; review their attachment. The Ground retains the canonical display capitalization pending a separate presentation decision.

[^T05-004]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S655, S656, S657, S658, S659, S660 (printed 455). S655 ངོ་བོ་ཉིད and S656 རང་བཞིན་ཉིད retain essence / intrinsic nature with the intensive itself. ཀ་དག་པས is the instrumental/causal primordial-purity construction; ལྷུན་གྲུབ remains spontaneous presence. S657 ས is locally grounds, an uncovered term, not the separate canonical The Ground for གཞི. S658 ལྟར་སྣང is provisionally seeming appearance; it is not the view entry merely because it contains ལྟ. S660 བབས་ཀྱིས་གྲུབ is tentatively established just as it settles; the subject is unexpressed and the precise force of བབས remains for review. No separate “spontaneous” term is imported.

[^T05-005]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S662, S663, S664, S665, S666, S667, S668, S669 (printed 456). At S662 ལུང is provisionally scriptural transmission and རིགས་པ is reasoning, distinct from awareness རིག་པ. S663 རྒྱུད is provisionally tantra in this textual list, rather than canonical continuum; མན་ངག is pith instruction. The exact scripture/continuity sense must be reviewed occurrence by occurrence. Short ལྟ / སྒོམ at S664 keep view / cultivation; the source order ends with activity. S666 is a compressed nominal relation, tentatively “as for its meaning, there is no accomplishment of a result”; S667 is deliberately “through phenomena ... becomes obscured” for ཆོས་ཀྱིས ... བསྒྲིབས, without silently changing phenomena to a positive liberating agent. ཆོས is a provisional standalone phenomenon/phenomena use, distinct from the established whole expressions dharma embodiment and nature of phenomena.

[^T05-006]: Golden-v1 chapter 5, S670, S671, S672, S673 (printed 456). སྦྱིན / ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས / བཟོད་པ are provisionally generosity / ethical discipline / patience. Their instrumental ending in S670 connects to S671, whose exact གནོད་དང་ཕན་འབྲས་བུ་བྲལ is rendered “free from the results of harm and benefit”; this is not a claim that the practices cause harm. S672 བསྒོམས་པས is a verbal/nominal cultivation form, not a new synonym. S673 མཆོག་ཏུ་བརྟགས is tentatively examined supremely; the object is implicit. Review the scope of the instrumental phrases and this superlative.

S1339 is a genitively expanded form of the established water lamp of the far-reaching lasso. The seeing/object relation in S1340 is tentative. Review the object relation and the lamp/appearance construction.

S1352 གཉིས་ཀའི་ཟུར identifies corners of “both” but does not explicitly name them; the bracketed subject of causing arising likewise remains open. “The pervading blue” retains ཁྱབ་བྱེད་མཐིང་ག rather than supplying an unstated colored entity. S1354–S1355 preserve the conditional and explicit five colors without naming them. Review the locative, the two referents and the cause of arising.

[^T06-041]: S1356–S1361 continue an apparent component explanation of ཤེས་རབ་རང་བྱུང. Fixed S1358 རབ་ཀུན་གྱི་རྩེ་མོར་གྱུར is retained as a “Rab” clause, rather than inserting a missing copula or syllable into the Tibetan. “Rang” exposes the self-component at S1359, and “Byung ba” the arising-component at S1360; their local meanings are proposals within the explanation, not replacements for the canonical whole lamp name or naturally arising primordial knowing. གཞན་ལྟོས is tentatively dependence on others, and མ་བཀག means unobstructed here. ལྷུག་པར retains letting be, while S1361 མ་འགགས retains the unceasing family. Review the compressed Rab clause and the component interpretation.

Its relation to the stallion, mental consciousness and movement remains unresolved; the dash shows the compressed join rather than supplying an unprinted verb. The five gates are not enumerated. S1367 “Lasso” and S1369 “Water” mark the expressly isolated ཞགས / ཆུ components. The nominal apprehended object and apprehending subject remain visible in S1367/S1368; གཟུང is provisionally verbal “apprehends,” not an approved general substitution for the nominal glossary entry. S1368’s object/subject genitives remain awkward and open. S1370’s “two” has no supplied identity. དངས་མ is provisionally “refined essence,” distinct from canonical essence for ངོ་བོ. Review the continuum/stallion join, the apprehension relation and the two portions.

That scoped proposal does not globally replace canonical “vajra chains,” which is retained for ལུ་གུ་རྒྱུད in S1376’s awareness exposition. S1373 བརྒྱུས is provisionally “strung,” a distinct form from canonical continuum; བཟོ་མཁས is a skilled craftsman, not silently the canonical contriver. S1374 preserves knowing and being aware as separate verbs. S1375 retains free from conceptualization and the negated staining relation. འབྲེལ་ཆགས is provisional “connected in succession,” and S1377 བུ་ག “opening”; no absent anatomy is supplied. Review the gold-chain exception and the relation of the opening to the path.

[^T06-044]: S1378–S1386: fixed འབྲས་བུ་རྣལ་བ་གཉིས་ཞེས་ཏེ leaves རྣལ་བ unresolved and retained; it is not changed to an expected maturation word or dropped. The next two lines name unripened saṃsāra and liberating embodiments and primordial knowing, but the relation between those members and the retained form remains open. The “four births” in S1381 are not enumerated by name; the following list gives classes of beings and should not be forced into a four-item count. S1386 makes their appearance as forms arise “from the unripened,” leaving its nominal referent open. The source spelling ཡི་དྭགས is preserved in records, distinct from earlier ཡི་དགས; both receive the provisional hungry-ghost sense. Review the retained result form, the twofold division and the scope of the four births.

[^T06-045]: S1387–S1392: the desire/hatred/pride/deluded-dullness/jealousy list preserves its stated order and “the like.” S1390 སྟོང་ཕྲག་དུ་མས་བསྡུས is tentatively “encompassed by many thousands”; no absent unit or exact count is supplied. S1391–S1392’s genitive relation is provisionally carried across the English lines: ordinary mind and the like qualify apprehended object and apprehending subject, while mental faculty and the like remain additional instrumental members. Their exact attachment is open; no protected mind term is replaced by generic mind. Review the numerical scope and genitive/instrumental chain.

[^T06-046]: S1393–S1404: མངོན་སྣང is provisional “manifest appearance.” The explicit five primordial knowings are not named. S1397 ཚིག / རྗོད་བྱེད are provisionally “utterances / what expresses,” kept distinct from canonical word for སྒྲ. S1398/S1399 preserve the place of primordial purity free from stains and the manifest-buddha predicate, with the unstated subjects marked where needed. S1402 retains the repetition of conceptual elaborations and being unelaborated, not an imported general emptiness claim. S1404 has bare འབྲིང, rendered “the middling”; it does not explicitly include the noun faculty from the glossary’s middling-faculty expression. Its relation to the path and various appearances remains provisional. Review the implicit subjects and the middling referent.

[^T06-047]: S1405–S1412: each gate, each truth-distinction, each knowing of an object, and each measure of realization retain the repeated distributive རེ་རེ. The ནས and ལས phrases are represented as “from,” and the knowing phrase remains instrumental. The subject of gradual seeing and attainment is implicit and bracketed. S1409 བརྟས is provisionally “increases”; the passage does not explicitly name any of the canonical four visions, so their names are not substituted. Great bliss remains the result and “the single secret of all buddhas” a tentative apposition. Review the repeated ablatives and the final apposition.

[^T06-048]: S1413–S1425: the result passage retains stain and purity as two, followed by entity and nonentity, rather than harmonizing the lists. The referents of དེ་དག, དེ and དེ་ཡི in S1413/S1416/S1418 remain unresolved; the English preserves the repeated “those/that/its” structure and the interrupted nominal pair. S1419 preserves empty then clear, followed by aware and unchanging; no reverse-order clarity-emptiness compound is imposed. S1420 མཚན་ཉིད is provisional “defining characteristic,” distinct from essence. S1423 རང་ལུས is “own body,” not automatically the embodiment entry. S1424 ཅོག་བཞག is a differently written attested form provisionally linked to leaving as it is; རང་སོ is provisionally “one’s own condition,” with its precise sense open. བསམ་གཏན retains this chapter’s provisional “meditative stability.” Review the result references, own-condition phrase and final nominal relations.

[^T06-049]: S1426–S1427: the colophon’s title is provisionally “the precious secret tantra String of Pearls.” རྒྱུད is an explicit occurrence-specific “tantra” proposal in a textual title, while S1364 retains canonical “continuum”; neither replaces the other globally. སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་སྣང་བ་ཐབས་ལ་མཁས་པ་བསྟན་པ is tentatively “teaching skill in means concerning the appearances of sentient beings.” The relation of appearances to skill in means is compressed and remains reviewable. The source explicitly numbers this chapter sixth. Review the title construction and attachment; the fixed colophon remains separate from the preceding root verse.

[^T06-L001]: Recurring technical forms in S1061–S1166: སངས་རྒྱས “buddha,” སེམས་ཅན “sentient being,” ཉོན་མོངས “affliction,” དྲི་མ “stain,” and བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས “Bhagavān” retain the opening provisional treatments. They do not establish new defaults or replace standalone ordinary mind. Explicit numbers and negations belong to their clauses; S1146’s instrument and S1152’s possessive interpretation remain separately flagged. Review these recurring whole expressions under the same unresolved terminology status as their first uses.

[^T06-L002]: S1061/S1065/S1066/S1072/S1119/S1121/S1122/S1165: unlisted བདེན is provisionally “truth,” ཉག་གཅིག “unique,” ཀུན་ཁྱབ “pervades all” or “all-pervading,” ལམ “path,” and ས “ground.” The source’s single/negative modifiers remain outside the bare truth gloss. “Ground” here does not silently substitute for the established The Ground assigned to གཞི. Review the local senses without importing named truth systems, paths or grounds.

[^T06-L003]: S1160/S1167/S1177/S1180/S1186: རང་བྱུང retains provisional “naturally arising”; the complete naturally arising primordial-knowing expression is absent here. In རང་དངས, དངས is provisionally “becoming clear” and རང supplies “by itself”; this is a clearing verb, not an automatic identification with canonical clarity or self-purified. Bare སྒྲོན་མ and ཞགས་པ are provisionally “lamp” and “noose.” No complete named lamp is supplied from those components alone. Review these forms and their local functions.

[^T06-L004]: Recurring forms in S1106–S1178: provisional ཡུལ “object,” ཆོས “phenomenon,” འཇིག་རྟེན “world/worldly,” འཁོར་འདས “saṃsāra and nirvāṇa,” འཁོར་བ “saṃsāra,” ཕུང་པོ “aggregate,” ཁམས “element,” སྐྱེ་མཆེད “sense base,” གཟུགས “form,” and nominal ལས “action” retain their local catalogue or bondage-sequence senses. “Element” in the constituent list remains distinct from “realm” in S1174. The broad object term does not acquire an absent focus/comprehension qualifier; nominal action remains distinct from the homographic ablative particle. Review these recurring proposals and the separately noted clause attachments.

[^T06-L005]: S1089/S1107/S1133/S1135/S1136/S1176: the short forms ལྟ and སྒོམ retain canonical “view” and “cultivation”; མ་རིག retains “ignorance.” Expanded བྱ་དང་བྲལ preserves “free from doing,” རྟོགས་དང་མ་རྟོགས preserves “realization and non-realization,” and རེ་དང་དོགས་པ preserves “hope and fear.” These grammatical realizations keep the established lexical families and source order; realization is not conflated with conceptual thought. Review the expanded constructions without changing the canonical assignments.

[^T06-L006]: Recurring local choices in this passage remain provisional: རྣམ་སྨིན “ripening,” སྡུག་བསྔལ “suffering,” ངན་སོང “lower destinies,” ཉོན་མོངས “afflictions,” སངས་རྒྱས “buddhas,” སེམས་ཅན “sentient beings,” འཇིག་རྟེན “worldly,” and ལམ “path.” The speech titles retain “holder of the vajra” for རྡོ་རྗེ་འཛིན and “Vajradhara” for རྡོ་རྗེ་འཆང. Both the full བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས and the actual short བཅོམ་ལྡན at S1273 are locally rendered “Bhagavān”; the missing final syllable in the short source form is not silently supplied to the source. Repetition does not confer glossary approval.

[^T06-L007]: In the category and constituent lists, provisional མི is the noun “humans,” not negation; ཕུང་པོ, ཁམས and སྐྱེ་མཆེད remain “aggregates,” “elements” and “sense bases.” The separate form འབྱུང་བ also has local “elements,” with five explicitly present at S1203 and S1256. The compressed བདེ་སྡུག་བཏང་སྙོམས at S1204 is “pleasure, suffering, and equanimity”; the short suffering component is not claimed as a separate approved glossary term. [^T06-L008]: The recurring unlisted forms retain local “saṃsāra” (འཁོར་བ), “liberated” (bare གྲོལ), “noose” (ཞགས་པ), “phenomena” (ཆོས), “object” (ཡུལ) and “light” (འོད); S1222 explicitly supplies its great modifier. Bare liberation does not import self-liberation or primordial liberation. S1212’s མཉམ་པའི “even” is a provisional form/application related to canonical evenness for མཉམ་ཉིད, not an exact headword match. Likewise, fixed ཅོག་བཞག at S1270 has local “leaving as it is,” while the canonical head is spelled ཅོག་གཞག. Neither local use approves a new canonical spelling.

[^T06-L009]: The purification series keeps local རྣམ་དག “completely purified,” without substituting self-purified or primordial purity. Full བདེ་བ་ཆེན་པོ is “great bliss,” while short དངོས is “entities”; neither is silently replaced in the source by a different headword spelling. ཀུན་ཁྱབ retains “all-pervading/pervades all,” གཟུགས “form,” and ཡི་གེ “letters.” S1251’s སྤྲོས་པ has provisional “conceptual elaborations,” with “without” supplied by overt མེད. S1283’s དྲི་མེད is adjectival “stainless,” related to earlier nominal stainlessness without an absent adventitious modifier. These remain local proposals.

[^T06-L010]: Expanded ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས retains the complete canonical “basic space of phenomena.” The short members ལྟ and སྤྱོད at S1231 retain “view” and “activity.” S1262’s separated སྤྲོས་དང་བྲལ preserves canonical “free from conceptual elaborations.” These are grammatical applications of the named canonical expressions, not new lexical assignments.

[^T06-L011]: The channel/exposition passage retains provisional ཀུན་རྫོབ “conventional,” འབྱུང་གནས “source,” གསང་ཆེན “great secret,” བདེ་བ “bliss,” བདེ་བ་ཆེན་པོ / བདེ་ཆེན “great bliss,” ཐབས “means,” དོན་དམ “ultimate,” རྒྱུ “cause,” ལམ “path,” and སངས་རྒྱས “buddhas.” མཐའ / མུ retain “extremes / limits,” and རྟག་ཆད “permanence and annihilation.” At S1315, “proliferating and gathering” for སྤྲོ་བསྡུ is a local alternative to chapter 5’s inactive “elaboration and withdrawal” proposal; it does not establish that the different canonical འཕྲོ་འདུ occurs here. གསང་སྔགས retains “secret mantra,” while bare གསང་བ and འོད at S1331 are “secrecy” and “light.” None of these recurring uses promotes a proposal to canonical status.

[^T07-051]: Location: S1683–S1686/S1690/S1702–S1704, printed515–516. Awareness without ordinary mind (སེམས་མེད་རིག་པ), body without phenomena (ཆོས་མེད་ལུས), teacher without phenomena (ཆོས་མེད་སྟོན་པ) and retinue of remembering and thinking without ordinary mind (སེམས་མེད་དྲན་བསམ་འཁོར) are provisional personified participants, not identifications with an unstated deity. The petitioner’s agency, the addressed body, the teacher’s speech and its emergence from objectless appearance remain distinct. Bare phenomena, body and object are local usages; ordinary mind and awareness retain their complete canonical terms. The opening question keeps both all expressions and primordial completeness in oneself. དྲན་བསམ is tentatively remembering and thinking; remembering is a contextual proposal beside canonical mindfulness, not its replacement. Review the title grouping, negative scope and supplied relation of the remembering/thinking retinue.

[^T07-052]: Location: S1688–S1691, printed516. The genitive phrase ཚིག་དང་ཡི་གེ་བརྡར་བཀོད་པའི qualifies ཆོས: phenomena set out as signs in words and letters is provisional, with the predicate there is no need kept on the next line. ཚིག is provisionally words and remains distinct in the record from canonical word for སྒྲ; letters and signs are uncovered technical usages. No names are added from a different canonical compound. Bare ཆོས is kept as phenomena here, without silently selecting Dharma or teaching. The following question retains that ordinary mind and this body without phenomena. Review the language/phenomena relation and the no-need predicate across the preceding page break.

[^T07-053]: Location: S1692–S1694, printed516. བེམ་པོས is provisionally insentient matter as the agent of cannot generate; the source supplies no explicit generated object, and none is added. Whether the noun concerns meanings or referents, and how the negated generation qualifies it, remain open. Review these relations without supplying an unstated object or converting every verb to arising.

[^T07-054]: Location: S1695–S1697, printed516. དེ་ཉིད་དྲན་བསམ་སེམས་མེད་ན is tentatively parsed as that itself has no ordinary mind that remembers and thinks. This takes དྲན་བསམ as qualifying ordinary mind; an enumerative attachment remains possible. Remembering is an explicitly provisional contextual treatment relative to canonical mindfulness, and thinking for བསམ does not silently establish conceptual thought or differentiating conceptualization. The conditional, question of difference, corpse in a charnel ground and alternative space comparison are all retained. [It is] supplies the last copula’s subject. Chief and grant me your word locally realize the petition’s གཙོ་བོས་བཀའ་སྩོལ; word here translates བཀའ, not སྒྲ. Review the emptiness relation and request formula.

Exact འདུས་ཚོགས་འབྱུང་བའི་ཕྱིར is tentatively because ordinary mind arises [from] a gathered collection; from marks a relation not separately case-marked. S1706 reads དྲི་མ་ཉིད་དང་ཡང་སྔགས་པས. The resulting instruction explicitly distinguishes ordinary mind and primordial knowing and assigns knowing the distinction to the learned. Review the unresolved causal/classifying syntax; the English does not claim the whole S1705–S1709 sentence is settled.

The two separately written predicates གཟུང་བ་ཡིན་ལ་འཛིན་པ་ཡིན retain apprehended object followed by apprehending subject. [^T07-059]: Location: S1721–S1725, printed517. Bare ཐུགས has no canonical assignment and remains visible unresolved; neither enlightened intent nor compassionate responsiveness is imported from another expression. བསྐྱོད་པ is tentatively stirring, with the causal པས preserved despite the unexpected connection to not being like insentient matter. Insentient matter is the same provisional བེམ་པོ treatment as in the question. The space comparison continues across metadata: སྟོང་གསལ་རིག་བཅས is tentatively empty and clear, endowed with awareness, retaining this order and the endowed-with relation rather than substituting a reversed clarity-emptiness compound. ཡེ་ཤེས་སྣང་བར་སྟོན is provisionally primordial knowing is shown as appearance; agency is unspecified and the appearance attachment remains reviewable. [^T07-061]: Location: S1732–S1733, printed518. The repeated དྲན family is kept as canonical mindfulness: mindfulness itself is without mindfulness, and primordial knowing is free of the very Ground of mindfulness. [^T07-062]: Location: S1734–S1736, printed518. Evidence: [Adzom p. 520, image 530](https://github.com/Lotus-King-Translation/Mu-Tig-Phreng-Ba/blob/main/evidence/golden/07/00530.png); Row3 right from ཞེས་མུ་ཏིག through row4 center བདུན་པའོ, before the next chapter dialogue.
